facts.statement: checkout and payment service:sli_error_ratio:rate5m both rise from about 0.136 at 15:38:47 to 0.395 at 15:40:47, with near-identical values.
The flag paymentFailure is on, with variant 50%.
Payment's server Charge error counter rises from 0 to 28 over the window, peaking at 15:41:22.
Payment warn logs show 30 lines, all 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold', first seen at 15:38:08. Payment has no error-level lines.
Error traces show checkout PlaceOrder and PaymentService/Charge failing with the same 'Invalid token' message, which propagates to frontend (http 422) and frontend-proxy.
Checkout has no error-level log lines in the window; its errors appear only as propagated spans.
Payment has one ReplicaSet revision (created 15:25:43, image 3.1.0-payment), so no deployment change occurred in the window.
The only Kubernetes warnings are readiness probe failures on alertmanager, otel-collector-agent and loki; none involve checkout or payment.

inferences.statement: The payment failures are injected by the paymentFailure flag, not by a code or deployment regression, because the flag is on and payment has not been redeployed.
Checkout is a victim, not the cause: its failing calls are to payment, and its own logs show no errors.

root_causes.cause: Feature flag paymentFailure is enabled at 50%, so about half of payment Charge calls fail with 'Invalid token'. Checkout's PlaceOrder then fails with 422/gRPC 13, which drives checkout's error ratio up to about 39.5%.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout's fast error burn (about 30-40% of requests failing) is caused by payment. Payment's server-side Charge spans are erroring at a rate that matches checkout's error ratio, with the message 'Payment request failed. Invalid token'. The feature flag paymentFailure is on at a 50% variant, which injects these failures. Payment's deployment has not changed since 15:25:43 (only revision 1), so the code is not the trigger. Checkout's own logs show no errors; its failures are the propagated payment errors.

alternatives.why_not: Payment has only one ReplicaSet revision (created 15:25:43) and no deployment change in the window, so there is no bad release to roll back to. Checkout has no errors of its own.
The failures are deterministic flag-driven injections, not a stuck or leaking process. Restarting payment would not stop the flag from injecting errors.
The problem is error injection, not a capacity shortfall. More replicas would still fail about half of Charge calls.

plan.no_action_reason: The fix is to turn off the paymentFailure feature flag in flagd (or set its variant to off). A human with flag-change rights should do this and confirm checkout's error ratio drops. Also confirm who switched the flag on at about 15:38, since the diagnosis lists this as unverified.
plan.summary: Checkout's fast burn is propagated from payment, where the paymentFailure feature flag (50% variant) injects 'Invalid token' failures on Charge calls. No available action fixes a feature flag, and payment has no release to roll back, so no action is proposed.

inferences.statement: The checkout alert is a downstream effect of payment's failures, not a separate fault in checkout.

root_causes.cause: The paymentFailure feature flag is on at 50%, so payment rejects about half of Charge requests with an 'Invalid token' error. Checkout and frontend then fail those orders.

diagnosis.summary: payment and checkout error ratios rose together from about 15:39Z and peaked near 36% and 35%. Error traces show payment's Charge failing with 'Payment request failed. Invalid token', and that error propagates up through checkout and frontend to frontend-proxy as HTTP 422. The only feature flag switched on is paymentFailure at 50%, which fits the failure rate. Payment has no error-level logs, so its failures are visible only in spans. Payment's single revision was created at 15:25:43Z, before the errors started, so a code deploy is not the trigger.

alternatives.why_not: payment has a single revision, created 15:25:43Z before the errors began, so there is no earlier good revision to return to and no bad release to undo.
The failures are deterministic 'Invalid token' errors triggered by a flag on 50% of Charge requests, not a stuck or leaking process. A restart would not change the flag and the errors would continue.
The errors are injected application failures, not a capacity shortage. More replicas would still reject about half of Charge requests.

plan.summary: Payment's error burn comes from the paymentFailure feature flag being on at 50%, not from a rollout or a stuck or under-provisioned process. No available action (rollout_undo, restart_deployment, scale_deployment) would fix it, so I propose none. A human should set paymentFailure to off in flagd for the lab environment, which should bring payment and checkout error ratios back to baseline.
